questions.prompt: Do you usually plan your days in advance or prefer to be spontaneous?
questions.sampleA1: I like... no plan. I like... do things... now.
questions.sampleA2: I don't plan. I like to do things now. It's more fun and I don't like to think too much.
questions.sampleB1: I don't usually plan my days. I prefer to be spontaneous. For example, if a friend calls, I can go out. However, sometimes it's good to plan a little, so you don't forget important things.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I'm a bit of a planner. I generally map out my day the night before, so I don't end up wasting time. That said, I always try to leave some room for the unexpected, because going with the flow now and then keeps life from feeling too rigid.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga... reja yoqadi emas. Menga... narsalarni... hozir qilish yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men rejalashtirmayman. Men hozir narsalarni qilishni yaxshi ko'raman. Bu qiziqarliroq va men juda ko'p o'ylashni yoqtirmayman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men odatda kunlarimni rejalashtirmayman. Men o'z-o'zidan bo'lishni afzal ko'raman.
Masalan, agar do'stim qo'ng'iroq qilsa, men tashqariga chiqishim mumkin.
Biroq, ba'zida biroz rejalashtirish yaxshi, shunda muhim narsalarni unutib qo'ymaysiz.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men rejalashtirilgandan ko'ra ko'proq o'z-o'zidan harakat qilishga moyilman. Rejalashtirishning afzalliklarini, masalan, samaradorlikni oshirishni tan olsam ham, o'z-o'zidan harakat qilishga ruxsat berish yanada qiziqarli va esda qolarli tajribalarga olib keladi deb bilaman. Albatta, muhim uchrashuvlar uchun oldindan rejalashtiraman, lekin asosan kunlarimni imkoniyatlar uchun ochiq qoldirishni afzal ko'raman.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Do you usually plan your days in advance or prefer to be spontaneous?
idioms: go with the flow - "oqimga tushmoq / sharoitga moslashmoq"
play it by ear - "vaziyatga qarab harakat qilmoq"
sentenceStarters: "I'd say I'm a mix of both…" - "Menimcha, men ikkisining aralashmasiman…"
"I like to have a rough outline…" - "Men taxminiy reja tuzishni yoqtiraman…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I'd say I'm a mix of both, but I generally lean towards planning. I like to have a rough outline of what I need to do each day, especially for work and important errands.
That said, I also enjoy leaving some room for spontaneous decisions, like meeting up with a friend or trying a new café. I think having a balance keeps life both organised and exciting.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Menimcha, men ikkalasining ham aralashmasiman, lekin ko'proq rejalashtirishga moyilman. Men har kuni nima qilishim kerakligi haqida, ayniqsa ish va muhim topshiriqlar uchun, taxminiy reja tuzishni yoqtiraman.

Shunga qaramay, men do'stim bilan uchrashish yoki yangi kafega borish kabi kutilmagan qarorlar uchun ham joy qoldirishni yaxshi ko'raman. O'ylashimcha, muvozanat hayotni ham tartibli, ham qiziqarli saqlaydi.

questions.prompt: Do you like visiting local markets or bazaars?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I like market. It is good.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like markets. I buy food and fruit. It is cheap and I like it because it is fun.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I like visiting local markets. I think it's interesting to see all the different things for sale. For example, sometimes you can find really unique souvenirs. Also, the food is often very good and it's a nice way to support local businesses.
questions.sampleB2: Yeah, I absolutely love them. There's something about the hustle and bustle of a local bazaar that a supermarket just can't match up to. I enjoy haggling over prices, and you can usually pick up fresh produce that's far cheaper. Plus, to me it feels like a really authentic slice of local life.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, menga bozorlar yoqadi. Men oziq-ovqat va mevalar sotib olaman. U arzon va menga yoqadi, chunki u qiziqarli.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, men mahalliy bozorlarga borishni yoqtiraman. Menimcha, sotuvda bo'lgan turli xil narsalarni ko'rish qiziqarli.
Masalan, ba'zida juda noyob suvenirlarni topishingiz mumkin. Bundan tashqari, ovqat ko'pincha juda mazali bo'ladi va bu mahalliy biznesni qo'llab-quvvatlashning yaxshi usuli.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men mahalliy bozorlar va bozorchalarga borishni yoqtiraman. Menimcha, ular odatiy do'konlarga qaraganda ancha qiziqarli xarid tajribasini taqdim etadi. Siz mahalliy madaniyatni haqiqiy his qilasiz va ko'pincha noyob, qo'lda yasalgan buyumlarni topishingiz mumkin. Bundan tashqari, bu kichik biznes va mahalliy hunarmandlarni qo'llab-quvvatlashning ajoyib usuli, bu menimcha juda muhim.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Do you like visiting local markets or bazaars?
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I absolutely love visiting…" - "Ha, men …ga borishni juda yoqtiraman…"
"There's something special about…" - "…da alohida bir narsa bor…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I absolutely love visiting local markets and bazaars. There's something special about the lively atmosphere — the colours, the smells, and the sounds of people bargaining.
I find it much more enjoyable than shopping in a supermarket because you can interact directly with the sellers and often get fresher produce. It also feels like a more authentic cultural experience, especially when travelling.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men mahalliy bozorlar va rastalarga borishni juda yaxshi ko'raman. Ularning jonli muhitida o'zgacha bir narsa bor — ranglar, hidlar va odamlarning savdolashish ovozlari.

Men uchun supermarketda xarid qilishdan ko'ra bu ancha yoqimliroq, chunki siz sotuvchilar bilan bevosita muloqot qilishingiz va ko'pincha yangi mahsulotlarni olishingiz mumkin. Bundan tashqari, bu ayniqsa sayohat qilganda, yanada haqiqiy madaniy tajriba kabi tuyuladi.

questions.sampleA2: Yes, I am a swimmer. I can swim in the pool. I like swimming, and it is fun.
questions.sampleB1: I think I am an okay swimmer. I can swim, and I am not afraid of the water. I learned when I was young. However, I am not very fast, and I don't swim very often.
questions.sampleB2: I'd say I'm fairly decent, yeah. I learned to swim as a kid, so I'm completely at home in the water. I wouldn't win any races, mind you, but I can hold my own and stay afloat for ages. To be honest, I mainly swim to wind down and cool off in the summer rather than to compete.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men suzuvchiman. Men basseinda suza olaman. Menga suzish yoqadi va bu qiziqarli.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, men yaxshi suzuvchiman. Men suza olaman va suvdan qo'rqmayman. Men yoshligimda o'rganganman.
Ammo, men juda tez emasman va men juda ko'p suzmayman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men o'zimni yetarlicha malakali suzuvchi deb ayta olaman. Men suvda o'zimni qulay his qilaman va juda charchamasdan ancha vaqt suza olaman. Garchi men hech qanday musobaqalarda g'olib bo'lmasam ham, o'zimni himoya qila olaman. Men asosan jismoniy mashq va dam olish uchun suzaman, ayniqsa yoz oylarida.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Are you a good swimmer?
idioms: sink or swim - "yo suzasan, yo cho'kasan (o'zing harakat qil)"
phrases: comfortable in the water - "suvda o'zini erkin his qilmoq"
sentenceStarters: "I wouldn't say I'm a particularly…" - "Men unchalik …deb ayta olmayman…"
"I learned the basics as a child…" - "Men asoslarini bolaligimda o'rgandim…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I wouldn't say I'm a particularly strong swimmer, but I can manage well enough. I learned the basics as a child and I'm comfortable in the water, whether it's a pool or the sea.
I don't swim competitively or anything like that, but I enjoy it as a way to cool off during the summer. I'd love to improve my technique someday, perhaps by taking proper lessons.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men o'zimni ayniqsa kuchli suzuvchiman deb ayta olmayman, lekin men yaxshi uddalay olaman. Men bolaligimda asoslarini o'rganganman va suvda o'zimni qulay his qilaman, xoh u basseyn bo'lsin, xoh dengiz.

Men musobaqa tarzida suzmayman yoki shunga o'xshash narsa, lekin yozda salqinlashning bir usuli sifatida bundan zavqlanaman. Men bir kun kelib texnikamni yaxshilashni xohlardim, ehtimol tegishli darslar olib.

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1:
I see map. And phone.

Map is paper. Phone is map too.
questions.sampleA2:
I see a map. It is a big paper map. And I see a phone.

The phone has a map too. I think the map is for travel.
questions.sampleB1:
In the pictures, I can see two ways to find directions. One is a paper map, which is quite large. The other is a phone with a map app.

I think the paper map is older. However, the phone map is more modern and probably easier to use.
questions.sampleB2: In the first picture, I can see a young tourist standing on a sunny street, poring over a large paper map. He's got a camera round his neck, so he's clearly trying to find his bearings the old-fashioned way. In the second one, there's a close-up of a hand holding a smartphone with a digital map and a red pin on the screen. The contrast is striking — one relies on a time-honoured method, while the other shows how we get around nowadays, with directions at our fingertips.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Men xarita ko'ryapman. Va telefon.

Xarita qog'oz. Telefon ham xarita.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men xaritani ko'ryapman. Bu katta qog'oz xarita. Va men telefonni ko'ryapman.

Telefonda ham xarita bor. Menimcha, xarita sayohat uchun.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Rasmlarda men yo'nalishlarni topishning ikki usulini ko'ryapman. Birinchisi qog'oz xarita, u ancha katta. Ikkinchisi esa xarita ilovasi bor telefon.

Menimcha, qog'oz xarita eskiroq. Biroq, telefon xaritasi zamonaviyroq va ehtimol ishlatish uchun osonroq.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Rasmlarda navigatsiyaga nisbatan ikki xil yondashuv tasvirlangan. Birida, kimdir an'anaviy qog'oz xaritadan foydalanmoqda, bu esa amaliyroq va ehtimol texnologiyaga kamroq bog'liq usulni ko'rsatadi.

Boshqasida esa, raqamli xaritani ko'rsatayotgan smartfon tasvirlangan, bu zamonaviy GPS texnologiyasining qulayligi va ommabopligini ifodalaydi. Bu usullarning qanchalik farq qilishini ko'rish qiziq, bu bizning atrofimizdagi dunyo bilan qanday munosabatda bo'lishimizdagi o'zgarishni aks ettiradi.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: old school vs new school - "eski usul va yangi usul"
sentenceStarters: "In the first picture, I can see…" - "Birinchi rasmda men ko'ryapman…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
In the first picture, I can see a person unfolding and reading a large, printed paper map while travelling. They seem to be trying to find their way in an unfamiliar place using a traditional method.
In the second picture, someone is looking at a digital GPS map on their smartphone, which represents the modern way of navigating. The contrast is clear — one shows a time-tested approach while the other reflects how technology has fundamentally changed the way we get around.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi rasmda men sayohat qilayotgan odam katta, bosma qog'oz xaritani ochib o'qiyotganini ko'ryapman. Ular an'anaviy usuldan foydalanib, notanish joyda yo'lini topishga harakat qilayotganga o'xshaydi.

Ikkinchi rasmda esa, kimdir smartfonidagi raqamli GPS xaritaga qarayapti, bu navigatsiyaning zamonaviy usulini ifodalaydi. Farq aniq ko'rinib turibdi — biri vaqt sinovidan o'tgan yondashuvni ko'rsatsa, ikkinchisi texnologiya bizning qanday harakatlanishimizni tubdan o'zgartirganini aks ettiradi.

questions.prompt: What are the advantages of using digital maps for navigation?
questions.sampleA2: I like maps on phone. It's easy to see. And I can find places. But sometimes no internet.
questions.sampleB1: Digital maps are useful. I think it's good because you can see where you are. Also, it shows you the way to go. For example, if I want to go to the shop, I use the map. However, sometimes the map is wrong.
questions.sampleB2: The biggest advantage, I'd say, is sheer convenience. Digital maps give you real-time traffic updates, so you can steer clear of jams and work out the quickest route in seconds. On top of that, they point out nearby cafés or petrol stations, which is genuinely handy when you're in unfamiliar territory.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menga telefondagi xaritalar yoqadi. Ularni ko'rish oson. Va men joylarni topa olaman. Lekin ba'zida internet bo'lmaydi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Raqamli xaritalar foydali. Menimcha, bu yaxshi, chunki siz qayerda ekanligingizni ko'rishingiz mumkin. Shuningdek, u sizga qayerga borishni ko'rsatadi. Misol uchun, agar men do'konga bormoqchi bo'lsam, xaritadan foydalanaman. Biroq, ba'zida xarita noto'g'ri bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Raqamli xaritalarning bir nechta afzalliklari bor.
Birinchidan, ular juda qulay, chunki odatda telefoningizda bo'ladi. Siz osongina yo'nalishlar va diqqatga sazovor joylarni topishingiz mumkin. Yana bir afzalligi shundaki, ular ko'pincha real vaqt rejimida tirbandlik haqida ma'lumot beradi, bu esa kechikishlarning oldini olishga yordam beradi.
Biroq, kamchiligi shundaki, ular barqaror internet aloqasiga bog'liq, bu har doim ham mavjud emas.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the advantages of using digital maps for navigation?
idioms: at your fingertips - "qo'l ostida / bir tugma narida"
sentenceStarters: "Digital maps offer a wide range of…" - "Raqamli xaritalar keng qamrovli…"
"The most obvious benefit is…" - "Eng aniq foyda shundaki…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Digital maps offer a wide range of advantages over traditional paper maps. The most obvious benefit is real-time navigation — apps like Google Maps can show your exact location, provide turn-by-turn directions, and even suggest the fastest route based on current traffic conditions.
This makes it virtually impossible to get lost. Another major advantage is that digital maps are constantly updated, so you always have access to the most accurate information about roads, landmarks, and public transport.
They also offer additional features like finding nearby restaurants, petrol stations, or attractions with just a few taps. For travellers, the ability to download offline maps means you can navigate even without an internet connection. As they say, "knowledge is power", and having all that information at your fingertips is incredibly empowering.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Raqamli xaritalar an'anaviy qog'oz xaritalarga nisbatan ko'plab afzalliklarni taqdim etadi. Eng aniq afzalligi - bu real vaqt rejimida navigatsiya; Google Maps kabi ilovalar sizning aniq joylashuvingizni ko'rsatishi, qadam-baqadam yo'nalishlarni taqdim etishi va hatto joriy transport holatiga asoslangan eng tezkor marshrutni taklif qilishi mumkin.

Bu adashib qolishni deyarli imkonsiz qiladi. Yana bir muhim afzalligi shundaki, raqamli xaritalar doimiy ravishda yangilanib turadi, shuning uchun sizda har doim yo'llar, diqqatga sazovor joylar va jamoat transporti haqida eng aniq ma'lumot mavjud.

Ular, shuningdek, yaqin atrofdagi restoranlar, yoqilg'i quyish shoxobchalari yoki diqqatga sazovor joylarni bir necha marta bosish orqali topish kabi qo'shimcha funktsiyalarni ham taklif qiladi. Sayohatchilar uchun oflayn xaritalarni yuklab olish imkoniyati internetga ulanmasdan ham navigatsiya qilish imkonini beradi. Aytishlaricha, "bilim - kuch", va barcha ma'lumotlarning qo'l ostida bo'lishi juda kuch beradi.

questions.prompt: Why might someone still choose to use a printed paper map today?
questions.sampleA1: I like paper map. It is big. I can see. Phone no work always.
questions.sampleA2: Maybe they like paper maps because they don't need battery. And maybe they don't have a phone. It is easy to read and you can see everything.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think some people use paper maps because they are reliable. For example, if your phone battery dies, the map still works. Also, it's easier to see a big area on a paper map than on a small phone screen. It's also good if you don't have internet.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the thing is, paper maps never let you down — there's no battery to run out and no signal to lose. Out in the countryside, where coverage is patchy, that reliability comes in handy. On top of that, a map gives you a bird's-eye view of the area, which I suppose a small screen can't. For some, there's a nostalgic charm to it as well.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men qog'oz xaritani yaxshi ko'raman. U katta. Men ko'ra olaman. Telefon har doim ishlamaydi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Balki ularga qog'oz xaritalar yoqadir, chunki ularga batareya kerak emas. Va balki ularda telefon yo'qdir. Uni o'qish oson va siz hamma narsani ko'rishingiz mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha, ba'zi odamlar qog'oz xaritalardan foydalanishadi, chunki ular ishonchli.
Masalan, agar telefoningizning batareyasi o'chib qolsa ham, xarita ishlayveradi. Shuningdek, qog'oz xaritada katta maydonni kichkina telefon ekraniga qaraganda ko'rish osonroq. Agar internetingiz bo'lmasa ham, bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Kimdirning bosma xaritani tanlashiga bir nechta sabab bo'lishi mumkin.
Birinchidan, ular texnologiyaga bog'liq emas; batareyaga ehtiyoj yo'q va uyali aloqa signaliga tayanilmaydi, bu esa olis joylarda juda muhim.
Ikkinchidan, qog'oz xarita yaxlit ko'rinishni taqdim etadi, bu sizga relyefni vizualizatsiya qilish va raqamli qurilmada aylantirishdan ko'ra samaraliroq marshrutlarni rejalashtirish imkonini beradi.
Bundan tashqari, ba'zi odamlar teginish tajribasini va marshrutni jismonan kuzatish jarayonini GPSdan foydalanishdan ko'ra qiziqarliroq va chalg'ituvchi emas deb bilishadi. Nihoyat, ba'zi vaziyatlarda, ayniqsa favqulodda vaziyatlarda, qog'oz xarita muhim zaxira navigatsiya vositasi bo'lib xizmat qilishi mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why might someone still choose to use a printed paper map today?
idioms: if it ain't broke, don't fix it - "buzilmagan narsani tuzatma"
sentenceStarters: "Despite the dominance of digital technology…" - "Raqamli texnologiyaning ustunligiga qaramay…"
"First of all, paper maps don't require…" - "Avvalo, qog'oz xaritalar talab qilmaydi…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Despite the dominance of digital technology, there are still valid reasons why someone might prefer a printed paper map. First of all, paper maps don't require a battery or internet connection, which makes them extremely reliable in remote areas where phone signal might be weak or non-existent.
Some hikers and adventurers specifically prefer them for this reason. Secondly, a paper map gives you a much broader overview of an entire region at once, allowing you to see connections between places that a small phone screen simply can't show.
There's also a nostalgic charm to unfolding a large map and planning a journey the old-fashioned way — it feels more like an adventure. Finally, for some older people who didn't grow up with technology, paper maps are simply more familiar and intuitive. As the saying goes, "if it ain't broke, don't fix it".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Raqamli texnologiyaning ustunligiga qaramay, kimdir bosma qog'oz xaritani afzal ko'rishining hali ham asosli sabablari bor. Avvalo, qog'oz xaritalar batareya yoki internet aloqasini talab qilmaydi, bu ularni telefon signali zaif yoki umuman bo'lmagan olis hududlarda juda ishonchli qiladi.

Ba'zi sayyohlar va sarguzashtchilar aynan shu sababga ko'ra ularni afzal ko'rishadi. Ikkinchidan, qog'oz xarita sizga butun mintaqaning ancha keng qamrovli ko'rinishini bir vaqtning o'zida beradi, bu sizga kichik telefon ekranida ko'rsatib bo'lmaydigan joylar o'rtasidagi aloqalarni ko'rish imkonini beradi.

Katta xaritani ochib, sayohatni eski usulda rejalashtirishning o'ziga xos nostaljik jozibasi bor - bu sarguzashtga o'xshaydi. Nihoyat, texnologiya bilan o'smagan ba'zi keksa odamlar uchun qog'oz xaritalar shunchaki tanish va tushunarliroq. Maqol aytganidek, "agar ishlayotgan bo'lsa, uni tuzatma".

questions.prompt: Describe a time you spoke or performed in front of an audience.
questions.sampleA1: I speak in school. I read a book. I am happy.
questions.sampleA2: I spoke in front of my class. It was about animals. I was nervous, but my teacher helped me. I liked it, and my friends clapped.
questions.sampleB1: Okay, I remember one time I had to give a presentation in my English class. It was about my favorite book. I was a little bit nervous at first, but I practiced a lot. I think it went well because my teacher said it was good. Also, some of my classmates asked me questions afterwards.
questions.sampleB2: Right, I'd like to talk about the first time I ever gave a proper speech in front of a big audience. It was at my university graduation, and I'd been asked to say a few words on behalf of my year group. To be honest, the moment I stepped up to the podium and saw all those faces, I got a serious case of butterflies in my stomach. My hands were shaking and my mouth went completely dry. But I'd gone over my notes dozens of times, so once I got the first sentence out, I gradually settled into it and even started to enjoy myself. By the end, my classmates gave me a warm round of applause, which felt absolutely fantastic. As for how it affected my confidence, I'd say it was a real turning point. Before that day, I used to shy away from any kind of public speaking, but pulling it off gave me a huge confidence boost. It taught me that a few nerves are perfectly natural and, if anything, they keep you on your toes. Ever since, I've been far more willing to put myself forward for presentations at work. As for why public speaking matters so much these days, I suppose it's because being able to get your point across clearly is priceless in almost any career. Whether you're pitching an idea to your boss or chairing a meeting, people who can think on their feet and speak with conviction tend to stand out. At the end of the day, ideas only carry weight if you can actually communicate them.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men maktabda gapirdim. Men kitob o'qidim. Men xursandman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men sinfim oldida gapirdim. Bu hayvonlar haqida edi. Men hayajonda edim, lekin o'qituvchim menga yordam berdi. Menga yoqdi va do'stlarim qarsak chalishdi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Xo'sh, esimda, bir marta ingliz tili darsida taqdimot qilganman. Bu mening sevimli kitobim haqida edi. Dastlab biroz hayajonlangan edim, lekin ko'p mashq qildim. O'ylaymanki, yaxshi o'tdi, chunki o'qituvchim yaxshi dedi. Shuningdek, ba'zi sinfdoshlarim keyin menga savollar berishdi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Esimda, bir marta ishda loyihani taqdim etishim kerak bo'lgan. Bu ancha katta yig'ilish edi, balki yigirmata odamcha, shu jumladan menejerim ham bor edi. Dastlab men juda xavotirda edim, chunki bu muhim taqdimot edi.
Shunga qaramay, men yaxshilab tayyorgarlik ko'rgan edim va materialimga ishonardim. O'ylaymanki, taqdimot muvaffaqiyatli bo'ldi va bu unumli muhokamalarga olib keldi. Bu menga professional muhitda taqdimot qilishda o'zimni yanada qulay his qilishimga yordam berdi.

vocabulary.title: Q7 - Describe a time you spoke or performed in front of an audience
idioms: the pen is mightier than the sword - "qalam qilichdan kuchli"
sentenceStarters: "I'd like to describe a time when…" - "Men bir voqeani tasvirlab bermoqchiman…"
"This experience had a tremendously positive…" - "Bu tajriba juda ijobiy ta'sir ko'rsatdi…"

bulletPoints: Describe a time you spoke or performed in front of an audience.
How did this experience affect your confidence?
Why is public speaking considered an important skill in modern society?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A time I spoke in front of an audience:
I'd like to describe a time when I had to give a presentation at a university conference in front of about a hundred people. I had prepared for weeks, but when I walked up to the stage, my heart was pounding with nerves. However, once I started speaking and saw the audience genuinely engaged, I began to relax and actually enjoyed the experience.
How it affected my confidence:
This experience had a tremendously positive effect on my confidence. Before that day, I used to dread any form of public speaking, but afterwards I realised that thorough preparation and practice can overcome even the worst stage fright. It taught me that being nervous is perfectly normal and doesn't mean you'll perform badly. Since then, I've voluntarily taken on more speaking opportunities, and each one has boosted my self-esteem further.
Why public speaking is important:
As for why public speaking is considered important in modern society, I believe it's because effective communication is essential in almost every profession. Whether you're pitching an idea to investors, leading a team meeting, or even having a job interview, the ability to articulate your thoughts clearly and persuasively is invaluable.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Auditoriya oldida nutq so'zlagan vaqtim:
Men yuzga yaqin odam ishtirok etgan universitet konferensiyasida taqdimot o'tkazishimga to'g'ri kelgan vaqt haqida gapirmoqchiman. Men haftalar davomida tayyorgarlik ko'rgan edim, lekin sahnaga chiqqanimda, yuragim hayajondan duk-duk ura boshladi. Biroq, gapira boshlaganimdan so'ng va auditoriyaning chin dildan qiziqayotganini ko'rganimdan keyin, men xotirjam bo'la boshladim va bu jarayondan rohatlandim.
Bu mening o'zimga bo'lgan ishonchimga qanday ta'sir qildi:
Bu tajriba mening o'zimga bo'lgan ishonchimga juda ijobiy ta'sir ko'rsatdi. O'sha kunga qadar men har qanday ommaviy nutqdan qo'rqardim, lekin keyin puxta tayyorgarlik va mashqlar hatto eng yomon sahna qo'rquvini ham yengishga qodirligini angladim. Bu menga asabiylashish mutlaqo normal holat ekanligini va bu yomon chiqish qilishingizni anglatmasligini o'rgatdi. O'shandan beri men ko'proq nutq imkoniyatlarini o'z zimmamga oldim va ularning har biri mening o'z-o'zimni qadrlashimni yanada oshirdi.
Nima uchun ommaviy nutq muhim:
Nima uchun ommaviy nutq zamonaviy jamiyatda muhim deb hisoblanishiga kelsak, menimcha, deyarli har bir kasbda samarali muloqot muhimdir. Investorlarga g'oyani taqdim etasizmi, jamoa yig'ilishini boshqarasizmi yoki hatto ishga suhbatga kirasizmi, o'z fikrlaringizni aniq va ishonarli tarzda ifoda eta olish qobiliyati beqiyosdir.

questions.sampleB2: This is a topic that tends to bring up strong feelings, and I can honestly see both sides of the argument. On the one hand, those who agree would say that young people owe it to their elders to look after them. After all, our grandparents and parents raised us and made sacrifices, so giving back is simply a matter of respect and gratitude. On top of that, caring for the older generation strengthens family bonds and passes on values like patience and empathy that you can't really learn from a textbook. As the saying goes, blood is thicker than water. On the other hand, the opposing view does hold some water too. Young people nowadays are often stretched thin, juggling studies, work and their own families, so piling caregiving on top can quickly lead to burnout. Some would argue that the state and professional care services ought to take on the bulk of that responsibility, especially since not everyone lives close to their relatives. Personally, I tend to sit somewhere in the middle. I firmly believe it should be a shared responsibility rather than falling squarely on young shoulders, and it certainly shouldn't be dumped entirely on the government either. Where they can, young people should pitch in — even a phone call or a weekly visit goes a long way — but they shouldn't have to give up their own lives entirely. At the end of the day, looking after the elderly is something society as a whole needs to chip in on.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a topic that touches on deeply held values about family and society. Those who believe young people should care for the elderly argue that it shows respect and gratitude for everything older generations have done — after all, they raised us, supported us, and made sacrifices for our future.
Taking care of them in return builds stronger family bonds and creates a mutual support system that benefits everyone emotionally. Furthermore, this responsibility teaches young people invaluable qualities like patience, empathy, and important life values that they might not learn elsewhere.
However, opponents make some reasonable points too. Many young people today are already under enormous academic and professional pressure, and adding caregiving duties could lead to burnout. Some argue that governments and professional care systems should bear the primary responsibility for elderly care.
Personally, I think it should be a shared responsibility. As the proverb goes, "it takes a village to raise a child", and I'd add that it takes the same village to care for its elders.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu mavzu oila va jamiyat haqidagi chuqur e'tiqodlarga tegishlidir. Yoshlar keksalarga g'amxo'rlik qilishi kerak, deb hisoblaydiganlar, bu keksa avlodlarning qilgan barcha ishlari uchun hurmat va minnatdorchilikni ko'rsatadi, deb ta'kidlaydilar — axir ular bizni tarbiyalashdi, qo'llab-quvvatlashdi va kelajagimiz uchun qurbonliklar qilishdi.

Ularga javoban g'amxo'rlik qilish oilaviy rishtalarni mustahkamlaydi va hamma uchun emotsional foyda keltiradigan o'zaro yordam tizimini yaratadi. Bundan tashqari, bu mas'uliyat yoshlarga sabr-toqat, hamdardlik va muhim hayotiy qadriyatlar kabi bebaho fazilatlarni o'rgatadi, bularni ular boshqa joyda o'rganmasligi mumkin.

Biroq, qarshi tomonlar ham o'rinli fikrlarni aytishadi. Bugungi kunda ko'plab yoshlar allaqachon katta akademik va professional bosim ostida, va g'amxo'rlik vazifalarini qo'shish charchashga olib kelishi mumkin. Ba'zilarning ta'kidlashicha, keksalarga g'amxo'rlik qilish uchun asosiy mas'uliyatni hukumatlar va professional g'amxo'rlik tizimlari zimmasiga olishi kerak.

Shaxsan men, bu umumiy mas'uliyat bo'lishi kerak deb o'ylayman. Maqolda aytilganidek, "bolani tarbiyalash uchun qishloq kerak", men esa keksalarga g'amxo'rlik qilish uchun ham xuddi shu qishloq kerak, deb qo'shgan bo'lardim.
